outcome: Incoming text retains the existing approved-knowledge answer path. Incoming voice becomes a bounded transcription event before entering that same path.
Automatic answers and explicitly sent human replies have separate text and audio outbox records containing the same answer. Text includes an AI-generated-voice disclosure.
Voice preparation, delivery and text delivery have independent states. Retry voice only never requeues the text parent. Uncertain customer sends are never blindly retried.

Inbox displays transcription/preparation and text/audio delivery states, polls pending work and offers authorized voice-only retries. Failed transcription retains the lead and requests human assistance. Automatic transcription failure sends one text request to resend or type when the current conversation still permits it.

migration.scope: Adds voice jobs, encrypted voice assets, paired outbox format and preparing state, tenant foreign keys, FORCE RLS, limited app-role grants and stale-work cancellation. Applied only to disposable local fixtures during this task.

processing.lanes: One generation, one dispatch, one transcription and one synthesis operation at a time per worker process. This is a global bound per process, not a cross-process distributed quota; provision one worker initially. Database leases prevent duplicate processing of a job.
processing.media: Compressed inbound limit 5 MiB; audio duration limit 60 seconds; PCM mono 24 kHz signed 16-bit. Reject invalid containers, silent audio, excessive duration and bytes. FFmpeg uses bounded pipes, explicit demuxers, no shell, pipe-only protocol, one thread and 20-second timeout.
processing.download: Graph metadata first, then exact HTTPS Meta media host allowlist, public address check, redirects disabled, size/checksum verification and 20-second deadline. No caller-supplied arbitrary URLs. DNS is checked, not socket-pinned.
processing.speech: Existing Runtime speech adapters, approved tenant speech-input/output capabilities and environment credential references. Existing speech model/voice configuration is reused. Each speech call receives a 60-second deadline; voice jobs lease for 3 minutes and permit at most 2 preparation attempts.
processing.delivery: Ogg/Opus by uploaded media ID. Audio dispatch waits until the text parent is accepted/delivered/read. Sending obeys current human/AI ownership, tenant authority, open reply window, opt-out, active lead and current release/provider/binding checks. Definite 429 responses retain bounded retry handling; ambiguous sends stay unknown.
processing.storage: Inbound compressed bytes and decoded PCM exist only in worker memory. Generated Ogg is AES-256-GCM encrypted in the tenant-scoped database, bound to tenant/message with AAD, until upload or 1-hour expiry. Plaintext buffers are cleared where owned. No plaintext media file is written. After successful media upload the local encrypted bytes are cleared and only the provider media ID remains. Provider media retention and existing database backup retention still apply.
processing.cleanup: Worker clears up to 100 expired encrypted assets per tick, normally every 60 seconds, and cancels audio pending longer than 24 hours. Cleanup requires the voice worker to run; shutdown does not erase database assets immediately.
processing.failure: Unreadable automatic voice input moves to human_requested and queues one safe text fallback. In human-owned conversations failures remain visible for staff. Retry control is limited to failed voice preparation with attempts remaining and unchanged eligible ownership; accepted/unknown/delivery-failed audio is not regenerated automatically. No transcript retry button is exposed; ask the customer to resend or use text.

steps: Apply migration 120 through the normal owner migration process before enabling voice.
Build Runtime (npm run build in sophia-runtime), deploy backend/frontend and restart the existing whatsapp:inbound-worker and whatsapp:reply-worker with matching profile configuration.

Configure the existing voice adapters in an approved orchestrated-voice experience for this tenant; bind speech-input and speech-output, publish and include that experience version in the WhatsApp agent release. Existing reasoning and published knowledge remain required for automatic answers.

Add voiceEnabled:true, mediaKeyEnv, transcriptionAdapter, transcriptionCredentialRef, synthesisAdapter and synthesisCredentialRef to the deployment-owned WHATSAPP_INBOUND_PROFILES entry. Use a distinct 32-byte hexadecimal media encryption key in the referenced server secret. Do not expose it to the browser. Retain the same key until encrypted assets have expired or been consumed.

Set WHATSAPP_VOICE_ENABLED=true only after migration, provider grants and test-number configuration. Existing inbound/reply worker, generation, outbound and automation flags still apply independently and default off.

Run a separately authorized test-number pilot for Spanish/English/Portuguese audio, delivery callbacks, latency, quality, opt-out, handoff and media playback before enabling the existing Business App number. Coexistence is not verified by this implementation.
deployment.rollback: Set WHATSAPP_VOICE_ENABLED=false in backend and workers to retain text replies and visible historical statuses. Queued audio will not dispatch. Keep migration 120 and the reply worker running: its bounded encrypted-asset cleanup lane runs even while voice generation is off. Do not rotate away the only active key while unexpired assets remain.
